text:
marco: Heads up — we're finalizing alert rules for the new runtime telemetry dashboard. Need quick alignment on thresholds and pager routing.
anya: Thanks. Can we start with which metrics are in scope? I have latency/err_rate/batch_util but not sure about kv cache or queue length.
dave: Key ones: runtime_request_p50/p95/p99, request_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, inference_queue_length, avg_batch_size. Also model_fallback_count for rollouts.
leila: Agreed. For dashboards we grouped into latency, errors, capacity. We should keep alerting conservative at first. Burn-rate alerts for SLOs + immediate pages for infra saturation.
marco: Proposal:
- Sev1 (page): request_error_rate > 0.5% over 5m OR inference_queue_length > 50 on any dedicated pool OR model_fallback_count spike > 10/min
- Sev2 (notify): p99 latency > 800ms sustained 10m OR kv_cache_hit_ratio < 60% for 15m
- Sev3 (channel only): p95 > 500ms for 30m or avg_batch_size < 1.2 indicating small batching
anya: That seems reasonable. For SLO burn-rate, we want to page when burn_rate > 6 for 1h? Or maybe faster for critical models.
dave: For platform SLO (99.5% availability) we usually page when burn_rate > 4 for 30m. For model-specific SLOs (customer-facing) maybe threshold 6 for 15m.
leila: Routing: Sev1 -> eng-sre primary pager, auto-escalate to eng-platform and eng-runtime after 15m. Sev2 -> slack notification to #eng-platform and a PD ticket assigned to oncall if not acknowledged in 30m. Sev3 -> #platform-ops only.
marco: Can we embed a small alertmanager receiver config? (draft)
marco: ```yaml
route:
  group_by: ["alertname", "pool"]
  receiver: 'team-routing'
  routes:
    - match:
        severity: 'sev1'
      receiver: 'pagerduty-sev1'
    - match:
        severity: 'sev2'
      receiver: 'slack-notify-sev2'
receivers:
  - name: 'pagerduty-sev1'
    pagerduty_configs:
      - service_key: 'REDACTED'
  - name: 'slack-notify-sev2'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#eng-platform'
```
anya: Looks good. We need runbook links in the alert annotations too. Can we use runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/runtime/overflow ?
dave: Yes add annotation runbook and playbook steps. Also add metric query examples for context:
- Error rate PromQL: `sum(rate(runtime_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_requests_total[5m])) * 100`
- Queue length: `sum(runtime_inference_queue_length)`
leila: For paging windows: business-hours vs 24/7? Dedicated customers expect 24/7 pages. Hosted non-critical can be business-hours only (8-6 PT).
marco: Good call. We'll tag alerts with customer_tier: dedicated|hosted and set routing to respect that.
anya: Quick question: who is owner for alert upkeep? I propose eng-platform owns the alert definitions, eng-sre owns pager schedule and escalation policies, eng-runtime owns metric instrumentation and dashboards.
dave: +1. Also add a monthly alert review checklist on the channel for triage.
marco: Can we agree on exact numeric thresholds in this thread so I can push them to the repo? I'll put conservative defaults and note them as editable per-pool.
leila: Defaults: request_error_rate sev1 0.5% (5m), p99 sev2 800ms (10m), queue_length sev1 50, kv_cache_hit sev2 60% (15m), model_fallback sev1 >10/min.
anya: I'll add a small test harness to simulate queued requests and validate alerts fire in staging.
dave: Also add synthetic traffic to exercise SLO burn alerts. Use `staging-load/redwood-synth` job.
sre-bot: NOTE: Oncall rotation for eng-sre updated this morning. Current primary: jules, secondary: tom. Escalation to eng-platform -> paged if not ack in 15m.
marco: Thanks. I'll make a PR with: alert rules + annotations (runbook + severity + owner) + routing config and link to grafana dashboard grafana/runtime/new-metrics.
leila: Please add a short changelog in the PR describing why thresholds chosen and where to tune per-customer.
anya: I'll coordinate staging tests, leave a comment in the PR with the test results.
marco: Plan: PR by EOD, staging validation tomorrow morning, roll to prod canary after 24h of green. 
leila: :thumbsup:
dave: Anything else before we lock defaults?
anya: Add an alert suppressor for known maintenance windows (billing migrations) — don't page during scheduled infra maintenance.
marco: Noted. I'll include silence schedule links and a maintenance label.
leila: Great, thanks team. If no objections I will merge once CI passes. :eyes:
